data: What is the final vector c^s derived from?

The final vector \( c^s \) is derived from the integration of multiple intermediate vectors \( c_1^t, c_2^t, c_3^t \). These intermediate vectors are themselves derived from the integration of smaller components \( T_1, F_1, FE_1, T_2, F_2, FE_2, T_3, F_3, FE_3 \), which are further derived from the input data \( P_1, P_2, P_3 \). The process involves a hierarchical integration of these components into the final vector \( c^s \).
